notes.text: Paul asked for a news style story off a Daily Star heatwave post. CHECKED FIRST: the Met Office is publicly pushing back on those headlines, saying a return to exceptional heat 'does not appear to be the most likely outcome' and that a heatwave is 'far from certain'. Local forecast for Sat 5 Sept is 20 degrees, which is below the 25 degree Leicestershire heatwave threshold. So the card carries the real forecast instead of the heatwave claim. If Paul still wants the heatwave angle it has to be framed as what the papers are saying, not as fact.

slots.title: Reactive: Met Office verdict news card
slots.caption:
Unbranded news card, no Merchants Yard logo. React to it in the app.

Suggested line over the top: sunny spells and 20 degrees will do us. Saturday, 2pm.

notes.text: Headline is the Daily Star's, credited on the card. Met Office is publicly disputing these headlines and Leicester is forecast 20 degrees Saturday, below the 25 degree heatwave threshold, so the credit line matters: it reads as what a paper said, not as something Merchants Yard is claiming. Background is a deliberate abstract heat gradient, NOT a drawn UK forecast map, because a made up map would imply real Met Office data.

Paul picked option I: 'Met Office verdict: more warm spells to come'. Accurate against the Metro piece, the Met Office long range forecast predicts brief warm or very warm spells early September. Deliberately no 25C figure: that is WX Charts for SOUTHERN England on 5 Sept, and Leicester is forecast 20C.

Background upscaled via Google Flow (Nano Banana 2, 0 credits). Winner crop-v1 measured 0.987 correlation against the real WX Charts map, so the geography is resolved rather than redrawn, and no labels, grid lines or invented coastline appeared. The full-map runs scored 0.29 to 0.60 and were discarded: forcing a 1.9:1 landscape map into Flow's 3:4 made it reframe and reinvent the forecast. Headline also reduced 74 to 58 for phone safety.

Font switched from Inter Bold to Poppins SemiBold to match the Daily Star reference card. Identified by letterform, not guessed: the reference has a single-storey geometric 'a', which rules out Inter and DM Sans and points to Poppins. SemiBold matches the reference weight, Bold read too heavy. Note this does NOT break the brand rule about Poppins being the kinda-chic set only, because this card is deliberately unbranded and is meant to read as a news outlet, not as Merchants Yard.
